items.informal_name: A non-zero scalar multiple of an algebraic element is integral
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {z : A},
  IsAlgebraic R z → ∃ y, y ≠ 0 ∧ IsIntegral R (y • z)
items.informal_description: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ be an $R$-algebra. If an element $z \in A$ is algebraic over $R$, then there exists a non-zero element $y \in R$ such that the scalar multiple $y \cdot z$ is an integral element over $R$.

items.informal_name: Characterization of algebraic elements over a reduced ring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {z : A} [IsReduced R],
  IsAlgebraic R z ↔ ∃ y, y ≠ 0 ∧ IsIntegral R (y • z)
items.informal_description: Let `R` be a reduced commutative ring and `A` be an `R`-algebra. An element `z ∈ A` is algebraic over `R` if and only if there exists a non-zero element `y ∈ R` such that the element `y * z` is integral over `R`.

items.informal_name: Existence of Integral Multiples in Algebraic Algebras Over Domains
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] [NoZeroDivisors R]
  [alg : Algebra.IsAlgebraic R A] (s : Finset A), ∃ y, y ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ z ∈ s, IsIntegral R (y • z)
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative ring with no zero divisors and $ A $ an algebra over $ R $ that is algebraic. For any finite subset $ S \subseteq A $, there exists a nonzero element $ y \in R $ such that $ y \cdot z $ is integral over $ R $ for all $ z \in S $. This means there exists a common nonzero scalar $ y $ that clears denominators to make all elements of $ S $ satisfy monic polynomial equations with coefficients in $ R $.

items.informal_name: Algebraic Element from Non-Nilpotent Scalar Integral Product
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {z : A} {y : R},
  ¬IsNilpotent y → IsIntegral R (y • z) → IsAlgebraic R z
items.informal_description: If $ y $ is a non-nilpotent element of a commutative ring $ R $ and the scalar multiplication $ y  ullet z $ is integral over $ R $, then $ z $ is algebraic over $ R $.

items.informal_name: Existence of Scalar Multiple as Product in Algebraic Extensions
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) {S : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S] [NoZeroDivisors S]
  [Algebra.IsAlgebraic R S] (a : S) {b : S}, b ≠ 0 → ∃ c d, d ≠ 0 ∧ d • a = b * c
items.informal_description: For any elements $a$ and nonzero $b$ in an algebra $S$ over a commutative ring $R$, where $S$ has no zero divisors and is algebraic over $R$, there exist elements $c \in S$ and a nonzero $d \in R$ such that $d \cdot a = b \cdot c$.

items.informal_name: Restriction of Scalars Preserves Algebraicity in Integral Extensions
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) {S : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Ring A]
  [inst_3 : Algebra R S] [inst_4 : Algebra R A] [inst_5 : Algebra S A] [IsScalarTower R S A] [NoZeroDivisors S]
  [int : Algebra.IsIntegral R S] {a : A}, IsAlgebraic S a → IsAlgebraic R a
items.informal_description: If $ R $ is an integral extension of $ S $ and an element $ a $ in $ A $ is algebraic over $ S $, then $ a $ is also algebraic over $ R $. This follows because the integral condition ensures that any polynomial relation over $ S $ can be lifted to a polynomial relation over $ R $.

items.informal_name: Integral Elements are Almost Integral with Scalar in Image
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S] {s : S},
  IsIntegral R s → (∃ t ∈ nonZeroDivisors R, t • s ∈ (algebraMap R S).range) → IsAlmostIntegral R s
items.informal_description: If an element $ s \in S $ is integral over $ R $, and there exists a non-zero element $ t \in R $ such that $ t \cdot s $ lies in the image of the canonical algebra homomorphism $ R \to S $, then $ s $ is almost integral over $ R $.

items.informal_name: An algebraic non-zero divisor divides a non-zero scalar
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S] {s : S},
  IsAlgebraic R s → s ∈ nonZeroDivisors S → ∃ r, r ≠ 0 ∧ s ∣ (algebraMap R S) r
items.informal_description: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $S$ be an $R$-algebra. Let $s \in S$ be an element which is algebraic over $R$ and is not a zero divisor. Then there exists a non-zero element $r \in R$ such that $s$ divides the image of $r$ under the canonical algebra map $\text{algebraMap} : R \to S$.
